summary: No security findings. No new trust boundary, input, dependency, network or storage (package.json changes only the test:slow script). Hidden information: the calling-range run is built from the same `attempts` (estimateOpponentRanges(view) / unseenCombos of hero+board) as the whole-range run, so advice still reads only the PlayerView; callingRange classifies combos against view.board only. Bots: every bot passes equity through adviceOptions + `options.equity ?? BOT_EQUITY`; recommendPostflop still takes ExactOptions<O, PostflopOptions>, so no style keys reach advice. Randomness: BOT_EQUITY uses equityWithBudget, seeded by deriveSeed, which reproduces fnv1a32(canonicalKey(c)) byte-for-byte (same ',', ';', '/' separators and card digits 0..51); sampling remains deterministic (not a fairness RNG; the deck shuffle is untouched). Bounded work: the exact path is gated by estimateEvaluations <= exactLimit (2,500 for bots); the sampled path keeps FEASIBILITY_NODE_LIMIT (100,000) and maxRejections = 100 * trials (50,000 for bots), and the narrower calling ranges in 9-opponent spots that exhaust it throw RangeError, which the A-7 catch turns into the whole-range number (non-RangeError errors still propagate, so it fails closed). The module-level callingRange memo is keyed by board and the canonical combo index, so stale entries cannot leak between boards. No worker files changed.
